dataset_example.question:
Analyze this web server log:
```
192.168.1.100 - - [10/May/2026:08:12:33] "GET /login.php?id=1' OR '1'='1'-- HTTP/1.1" 200 4521
192.168.1.100 - - [10/May/2026:08:12:35] "GET /login.php?id=1' UNION SELECT username,password FROM users-- HTTP/1.1" 200 892
192.168.1.100 - - [10/May/2026:08:12:37] "GET /login.php?id=1'; DROP TABLE sessions;-- HTTP/1.1" 500 234
```
dataset_example.answer:

Severity: HIGH
Evidence: Multiple SQL injection payloads in URL parameters including UNION SELECT, OR-based tautology, and DROP TABLE attempts. The 500 error on the last request indicates potential successful injection.
Mitigation: 1) Use parameterized queries/prepared statements. 2) Implement WAF rules to detect SQL injection patterns. 3) Apply input validation and sani

items.answer:
Attack Type: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) - Stored XSS
Severity: HIGH
Evidence: Malicious JavaScript injected into user-generated content (comment section), cookie theft via Image object and onerror event handler, external data exfiltration to evil.com domain.
Mitigation: 1) Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers. 2) Sanitize all user input before rendering. 3) Use HttpOnly and Secure flags on cookies. 4) Apply output encoding/escaping. 5) Use DOMPurify or similar sanitization libraries.

items.answer:
Attack Type: DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) - SYN Flood
Severity: CRITICAL
Evidence: Massive volume of SYN packets from distributed IP range, escalating traffic rate, server resource exhaustion (CPU 99%, memory), service degradation to complete outage, legitimate user impact.
Mitigation: 1) Deploy DDoS mitigation service (Cloudflare, AWS Shield). 2) Implement SYN cookies and rate limiting. 3) Configure network-level flood protection. 4) Set up traffic scrubbing and blackhole routing for attack traffic.
